title: Pulleys
unit: IAL Mechanics (M1) (unit inferred from file name)

questions.question: Particle P of mass m hangs vertically below a small smooth light pulley fixed at the edge of a rough horizontal table. Particle Q of mass m is on the table, joined to P by a light inextensible string passing over the pulley. The coefficient of friction between Q and the table is mu, where mu < 1. Q is released from rest, and the tension in the string before Q hits the pulley is kmg. Find k in terms of mu.
steps: Q on the table (towards the pulley): T - mu*m*g = m*a
P (vertically down): m*g - T = m*a
Add the two equations: m*g - mu*m*g = 2*m*a, so a = g(1 - mu)/2
Substitute into P: T = m*g - m*g(1 - mu)/2

questions.question: Q is initially a distance d from the pulley. Find, in terms of d, g and mu, the time taken by Q after release to reach the pulley.
steps: From part (a), Q (and P) move with constant acceleration a = g(1 - mu)/2
Using s = ut + (1/2)at^2 with u = 0 and s = d: d = (1/2)*a*t^2
t = 2*sqrt(d/(g(1 - mu)))

questions.question: Describe what would happen if mu >= 1, giving a reason for your answer.
questions.answer: Q stays at rest, because the maximum friction mu*m*g is at least m*g, which balances the pull of P.
steps: P hangs in equilibrium, so the string pulls Q towards the pulley with force m*g
The maximum friction on Q is mu*m*g
If mu >= 1 then mu*m*g >= m*g
Friction can hold Q, so Q does not move and the system stays at rest

questions.question: Block A of mass m is on a rough plane inclined at angle alpha to the horizontal, with tan alpha = 7/24 and coefficient of friction mu = 1/3. A light inextensible string runs from A up the line of greatest slope to a small smooth pulley at the top, then vertically down to block B of mass km. The system is released from rest, A moves up the plane and the tension is 4mg/3. (i) Find the magnitude of the acceleration of A in terms of g. (ii) Find k.
steps: sin alpha = 7/25 and cos alpha = 24/25
Friction on A acts down the plane: mu*m*g*cos alpha = (1/3)(24/25)mg = 8mg/25
A (up the plane): T - mg sin alpha - 8mg/25 = m*a, so T - 3mg/5 = m*a
B (down): km*g - T = km*a, so km(g - a) = T
g - a = 4g/15, so km(4g/15) = 4mg/3, giving k = 5

questions.question: Find the magnitude of the resultant force exerted on the pulley by the string, giving your answer in terms of m and g.
steps: Tension in both parts of the string is T = 4mg/3
Part to A is down the plane, direction (-cos alpha, -sin alpha); part to B is vertically down, direction (0, -1)
Resultant = T(-24/25, -32/25), with magnitude T*sqrt(576 + 1024)/25 = 8T/5
Magnitude = (8/5)(4mg/3) = 32mg/15

questions.question: Particle A of mass 2m rests on a rough plane inclined at alpha with tan alpha = 3/4. A light inextensible string runs from A parallel to a line of greatest slope up to a small smooth light pulley P at the top, then vertically down to particle B of mass 3m, which hangs freely. The coefficient of friction between A and the plane is 1/2. A is released and moves up the plane. For the motion before A reaches the pulley: (i) write down an equation of motion for A, (ii) write down an equation of motion for B.
steps: sin alpha = 3/5 and cos alpha = 4/5
A (up the plane): T - 2mg(3/5) - (1/2)(2mg)(4/5) = 2ma
Simplify: T - 6mg/5 - 4mg/5 = 2ma, so T - 2mg = 2ma (i)
B (vertically down): 3mg - T = 3ma (ii)

questions.question: Find, in terms of g, the acceleration of A.
steps: Add equations (i) and (ii) to remove T: 3mg - 2mg = 2ma + 3ma
mg = 5ma
a = g/5

questions.question: Find the magnitude of the force exerted on the pulley by the string.
steps: From (ii): T = 3mg - 3ma = 3mg - 3mg/5 = 12mg/5
Part AP points down the plane, direction (-4/5, -3/5); part PB points vertically down, direction (0, -1)
Resultant = T(-4/5, -8/5), magnitude T*sqrt(16 + 64)/5 = 4 sqrt(5) T/5
Magnitude = (12mg/5)(4 sqrt(5)/5) = 48 sqrt(5) mg/25

questions.question: State how you have used the information that P is a smooth pulley.
questions.answer: A smooth pulley gives no friction, so the tension T is the same on both sides and the same T appears in both equations.
steps: A smooth pulley exerts no frictional force on the string
So the tension is unchanged as the string passes over P
Hence the same T is used in equations (i) and (ii)

questions.question: Write down an equation of motion for Q, where Q (mass m) lies on a smooth horizontal plane and is joined by a string over a smooth pulley to particle P (mass 4m) on a rough inclined plane.
questions.answer: T = m*a (Q accelerates towards the pulley)
steps: The only horizontal force on Q is the tension T, directed towards the pulley
Q has mass m and acceleration a towards the pulley
So T = m*a

questions.question: For P (mass 4m) on a fixed rough plane inclined at alpha with tan alpha = 3/4 and coefficient of friction 1/4, and Q (mass m) on a smooth horizontal plane, the system is released from rest with P moving down the plane. Find, in terms of m and g, the tension in the string.
steps: sin alpha = 3/5 and cos alpha = 4/5, so normal reaction on P = 4mg(4/5) = 16mg/5
Friction on P acts up the plane: (1/4)(16mg/5) = 4mg/5
P (down the plane): 4mg(3/5) - 4mg/5 - T = 4ma, so 8mg/5 - T = 4ma
Q: T = m*a, so 8mg/5 = 5ma

questions.question: Find the magnitude of the force exerted on the pulley by the string.
steps: Both parts of the string have tension T = 8mg/25
Part to P: down the plane, direction (-4/5, -3/5); part to Q: horizontal towards Q, direction (1, 0)
Magnitude = T*sqrt(1 + 9)/5 = T sqrt(10)/5 = (8mg/25)(sqrt(10)/5) = 8 sqrt(10) mg/125

questions.question: State where in your working you have used the information that the string is light.
questions.answer: The tension is the same throughout the string, so the same T acts on P and on Q.
steps: A light string has no mass, so there is no net force on the string itself
Hence the tension is the same at both ends of the string
So the same T appears in the equation for P and the equation for Q

questions.question: Particle A (2 kg) rests on a rough plane inclined at alpha with tan alpha = 3/4, and coefficient of friction 1/4. A light inextensible string runs from A parallel to a line of greatest slope over a small smooth pulley at the top of the plane, then down to particle B (4 kg) hanging vertically below the pulley. The system is released from rest with the string taut and B descends. Find the tension in the string as B descends.
steps: sin alpha = 3/5 and cos alpha = 4/5; friction on A (down the plane) = (1/4)(2g)(4/5) = 2g/5
A (up the plane): T - 2g(3/5) - 2g/5 = 2a, so T - 8g/5 = 2a
B (down): 4g - T = 4a
Add: 4g - 8g/5 = 6a, so a = 2g/5

questions.question: On hitting the ground, B immediately comes to rest. Given that A comes to rest before reaching the pulley, find in terms of h the range of possible values of d, where A is initially d m from the pulley and B is h m above the ground.
steps: While B falls h, a = 2g/5, so speed squared at impact = 2(2g/5)h = 4gh/5, and A has moved up h
After B stops the string goes slack and A decelerates at g sin alpha + (1/4)g cos alpha = 3g/5 + g/5 = 4g/5
Further distance up the plane = (4gh/5)/(2 x 4g/5) = h/2
Total distance up the plane before A is at rest = h + h/2 = 3h/2
A must stop before reaching the pulley, so d > 3h/2

questions.question: State one physical factor, other than air resistance, that could be taken into account to make the model described above more realistic.
questions.answer: Friction at the pulley axle (the pulley is modelled as smooth), or the mass of the string (modelled as light).
steps: The model treats the pulley as smooth and the string as light
Friction at the pulley bearing would reduce the effective tension
Alternatively, the mass of the string would change the forces on A and B
Any one such factor is an acceptable answer
